changes.before: Return an immutable snapshot rather than sharing mutable actor-owned state.
changes.after: Return a snapshot that keeps its value after the original data changes.

before: An actor isolates its mutable state. Code outside it normally uses await to call its isolated methods.
Sendable describes values that can safely cross concurrency boundaries. It is a compiler-checked promise, not a lock added at runtime.
An immutable value-type snapshot containing Sendable fields is a simple way to communicate state without exposing a shared mutable object.
After await, other work may have changed an actor. A snapshot describes the state when it was made; it is not a live view.
For the exercise, snapshot returns CountSnapshot(total: total). The first result remains 3 after the store changes to 7; the second reports 7.
Do not add @unchecked Sendable just to silence a diagnostic. It bypasses compiler verification and requires a separate safety argument.
after: A snapshot is a value saved from one moment. It does not keep following later changes. This lesson returns a small, fixed copy of an actor's data.
An actor protects its changing data from unsafe access by other work. Code outside it normally uses await to call a protected method. await marks a place where that call may pause.

Sendable means a value can safely pass between separate pieces of concurrent work. Concurrent work can make progress during overlapping periods. Swift checks this promise; Sendable does not add a lock or make a value update itself.
Reading saved.text reads the snapshot, not the actor's current storage. Other work may change an actor while a call is paused. A returned snapshot still describes the moment it was made.
Complete snapshot in the count store by returning CountSnapshot(total: total). A snapshot taken at 3 must stay 3 after the store changes to 7. A new snapshot should report 7.
Keep Sendable's normal checks. @unchecked Sendable asks Swift to trust a safety promise it has not fully checked. This exercise does not need that shortcut.

before.question: A Sendable snapshot was returned with total 3. The actor later changes its total to 7. What should the old immutable value show?
choices: 3; it is a snapshot, not shared mutable actor storage
7; Sendable makes every value a live view
A compiler error because values cannot cross actors
before.explanation: The immutable struct carries a value copied out of the actor. Sendable permits safe transfer; it does not turn it into a live subscription.

after.question: A snapshot has total 3. The actor later changes to 7. What should the old snapshot show?
after.explanation: A snapshot saves a value from one moment. It is not a live view of the actor.

changes.before: Use Swift 6 language mode for the stated Sendable checking. Compiler version, language mode and an Xcode project’s isolation defaults are distinct settings. Do not add @unchecked Sendable to bypass the contract.
changes.after: Use Swift 6 language mode for this exercise's concurrency checks. The installed compiler version and the project's language mode are separate settings. The example also needs a program setup that allows top-level await.

project.title: Send a value across an isolation boundary
project.task: Return CountSnapshot(total: total) from the actor. Keep the snapshot immutable so earlier results stay unchanged after later updates.
project.done_when: The first snapshot stays at 3 and the later snapshot reports 7.
